PRODUCTION, INCOME AND FINANCE

GDP income and TFP

Year 40

Firm-technology TFP index

—

Capital-weighted firm technology in this model, normalised to 100 at opening. This is the technology component of productivity. The national PWT measure and the model’s output-based residual are different measures.

Labour income is the gross wage bill, including paid research. Gross capital income is operating surplus before interest, profit tax and depreciation, including business research subsidies. The two income shares use their combined total: GDP income excluding net taxes. Taxes and subsidies remain in the separate market-price GDP and government accounts. Interest, dividends and direct taxes redistribute income and are not counted as extra GDP. Negative income components are retained.

Government surplus and assets

Payment defaults, restructurings and exits

Restructuring keeps a firm operating after its debt is reduced. With firm exit enabled, default normally closes the firm instead. A restructuring required by the minimum-firm numerical limit is reported separately in the event log.

PURCHASING POWER

Prices and inflation

Choose Money & prices to try a spending-speed shock. Use the charts to compare the price level with real production.

Money and spending in the final year

How prices change

The price signal compares opening household and business money multiplied by spending velocity with the goods produced in the previous year. Faster spending or more money at the same output adds to price pressure. More output at the same spending power eases it.

The central bank’s target guides its rate decisions. Consumer inflation measures the annual change in prices including VAT. The consumer price index opens at 100, and average annual inflation compounds the change from year 0 to the final year.

MONETARY POLICY & FOREIGN ACCESS

Interest rates and the currency

Choose Policy & currency to run the experiment.

How the channels work

The central bank responds to last year’s inflation with a zero nominal-rate floor. For sustained very low inflation near that floor, it can buy existing public bonds by creating reserves and matching seller deposits where appropriate. A higher policy rate slows spending and raises business borrowing costs. The currency tends to weaken when the policy rate after inflation falls below the foreign basket’s real rate. You can also set a currency shock.

The currency index starts at 100. Below 100 means weaker against the modeled foreign basket. Depreciation puts upward pressure on prices and reduces the chance of reaching foreign technology. The opposite applies to appreciation. Imported production costs feed partly into domestic producer prices, reducing some of the real-price advantage of depreciation. The strength is an editable assumption; a neutral current account is not imposed.

NATIONAL ACCOUNTS

Saving − investment = current account

Investment here means fixed investment plus changes in inventories. Buying shares or bonds finances activity through a separate financial transaction. In this model, the current account equals goods exports minus imports plus household foreign investment income. Figures are rounded.

Saving by domestic sector
OUTSIDE THE DOMESTIC ECONOMY

Foreign sector

Foreign markets ↔ Domestic economy

Trade and real exchange rate

Real currency strength compares local producer prices with the foreign basket priced in domestic currency. Above 100 means local goods are relatively dearer than at opening. Trade orders respond to the real exchange rate and the technology of domestic firms relative to foreign competitors. Sellers fill the highest price bids first.

Net foreign assets follow the current account

Change in net foreign assets = current account = saving − investment

Net foreign assets are foreign assets minus foreign liabilities at acquisition cost. Their annual change is calculated from settled payments and must equal the current account. It cannot be set separately. Household portfolio choices change who holds the assets, not this national total.

Currency gains and losses are shown separately. The position at the current exchange rate equals net foreign assets at acquisition cost plus cumulative currency valuation. Gross settlement assets and funding start from a matched, empirically scaled stock and roll over. They stay positive in surplus and deficit years. The model assumes no separate capital transfers.

Import tariffs

Set Import tariff in the economy controls or choose the Import tariff experiment. Duty raises the price of imported goods. Households pay it to government, and VAT applies to the duty-inclusive price. Foreign exporters receive the border value. Real GDP uses opening tax rates so a tariff increase does not mechanically count as extra real production.

Household investments abroad

Annual paths, coverage and source definitions ↓

Foreign technology

Foreign donor inputs, indices and adoption by source
SourceTFP anchor / homeApplied annual TFP growthClosing donor meanDelayed donor benchmarkContactsAdoptionsWeighted gain

Penn World Table productivity anchors the three donors at opening. Their growth follows the selected projection or fixed-rate mode above; the donor mean also includes the assumed leader premium. The rest-of-world pool excludes the USA and China and the home economy or home-area members. The named foreign pools do not overlap. Each contact draws a technology opportunity around the delayed donor benchmark. A firm can benefit from an individual contact even when the source’s average is lower.

WHO RECEIVES THE INCOME AND HOLDS THE WEALTH?

Household inequality

Year 40

Income inequality over time

Financial wealth inequality over time

Gini measures how unequally a total is shared. Zero means equal amounts for everyone; higher values mean more inequality. Scenario is green; reference is dashed grey. The highlighted line marks the selected year.

Recorded financial wealth includes deposits, government and corporate bonds, paid-in shares in active firms, and foreign securities at the current exchange rate. Funded pension claims are included. Housing and mortgages appear separately in recorded net wealth; unpriced original household firm/bank ownership remains outside this measure. These distributions are simulated, not survey estimates.

Income and wealth by household group

Each column ranks households separately by income or wealth. A group contains 20% of households. The same households need not belong to the same group in both rankings.

Share of the total and average amount in each group
Ranked groupIncome shareAverage incomeWealth shareAverage wealth

Debt relative to GDP

Public debt includes claims held by households, the financial sector, the central bank and foreign creditors. Private debt includes modelled active business loans, corporate bonds and household mortgages. Deposits and shares are excluded to avoid double counting private borrowing.

    What policy could take from this run

      A research simulation, with explicit assumptions. Opening inputs use country-specific Eurostat, PWT, Federal Reserve, OECD, NBS, UN and matched central-bank data. Some pension observations are older; missing inputs are labelled assumptions. Foreign paths use OECD’s 2025/2026 projection vintage. Sources were retrieved in November 2026. Firm behavior and innovation returns are assumptions. The new ABM has no demonstrated out-of-sample forecasting accuracy.

      How timing and effects combine

      The full effect lasts for the selected duration, including the start year. Afterward, 0% ends it immediately, 50% halves it each following year, and 100% keeps it in place. Overlapping percentage shocks multiply. Rate, currency and foreign TFP growth offsets add. The model’s constraints and policy responses still apply.
